brief: A black cat on the homepage first screen faces the visitor and its eyes follow the pointer. Its tail runs down behind the page and peeks out at the very bottom; pull it too hard and the page snaps back to the top while the cat jumps in fright. Round 2: graphic, not realistic. The page itself stays as it is.

candidates.name: 01 Silhouette cat
candidates.concept: One solid ink shape with designed curves, almond eyes cut out of it; closest to the first SVG, drawn properly this time.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated flat silhouette, traced to SVG with potrace
Sits on the hero rule in the gap between the words and the photo
Tail hangs behind the rule and is clipped there
Slit pupils sit behind the shape and show through the eye holes
Ears, head and tail are separate paths, so startle can be animated

candidates.name: 02 One-line cat
candidates.concept: A cat drawn in the same thin line as the page's rules; its tail lands on the hero rule and becomes the rule.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated one-line drawing, traced to SVG; tail redrawn in code
Sits on the hero rule; tail runs right along it and fades from ink into the rule's grey
The page's own lines are the tail, so pulling it at the bottom reads literally
Round pupils inside small ring eyes
Lightest presence of the three; reads as outline, not a black cat

candidates.name: 03 Pixel cat
candidates.concept: A 20-cell-wide 1-bit icon, like an early Mac system icon or a Kindle screensaver sprite.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated pixel art, resampled to a clean 20x51 grid, 5px cells
Sits on the baseline of the lit word; can hop as the three frames rotate
Pupils are one-cell blocks that jump cell by cell
Startle swaps to a second sprite through the site's e-ink refresh flash
Most playful; strongest tie to the e-ink concept
